item.mechanism: Silicon diffusion from the silicide coating into the RHEA substrate drives the silicide layer inward, increasing the coating thickness while maintaining its double-layer structure.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with a Si-20Cr-20Fe fused slurry silicide coating
item.operating_conditions: High-temperature oxidation at 1000 °C and 1300 °C for 1 hour in static atmosphere
item.supporting_observation: The thickness of the silicide layer (L2) more than doubled after oxidation, and the layer moved toward the substrate.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism was observed at 1000 °C and 1300 °C; the text does not explicitly state if it holds at temperatures below 1000 °C or above 1300 °C.
quotes: Under high-temperature oxidation conditions, the silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred.
The silicide layer moved toward the inside of the substrate, led to the increase of its thickness.
The silicon element diffused into the MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate at high temperatures, and the siliconized layer moved toward the substrate.

item.mechanism: The initial coating forms a double-layer structure due to thermodynamic stability differences, where disilicide (MSi2) forms on the surface and lower silicide (M5Si3) forms at the interface.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate coated with Si-20Cr-20Fe slurry
item.operating_conditions: Fused slurry method: held at 1430 °C for 1 hour under vacuum (5 × 10⁻³ Pa)
item.supporting_observation: The outer layer has ~66% Si (consistent with MSi2) and the inner layer has ~38% Si (consistent with M5Si3), supported by Gibbs free energy analysis.
item.scope_limits: The text notes that Fe silicide was not detected by XRD, suggesting this specific phase formation logic may not apply to Fe.
quotes: The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a high silicon content layer mainly composed of MSi 2 as the outer layer and a low silicon content layer mainly contained M 5 Si 3 as the inner layer.
It indicated that the silicide tended to bind more silicon and disilicide had the best stability.
The difference of the Gibbs free energies between MSi2 and 1/5M 5 Si 3 (M = Ta and Ti) was very smaller than those of other elements.

item.mechanism: Oxide layer structure and composition depend strongly on oxidation temperature, with higher temperatures promoting complete oxidation and a double-layer oxide structure.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating
item.operating_conditions: Oxidation at 1000 °C (single-layer oxide) and 1300 °C (double-layer oxide) for 1 hour
item.supporting_observation: At 1000 °C, the oxide layer is a single layer of complex oxides; at 1300 °C, it splits into a low-oxygen layer (L3) and a complete oxide layer (L4).
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is specific to the temperature range of 1000–1300 °C; the text does not cover behavior outside this range.
quotes: The structure and compositions of the oxide layer on the outer surface strongly depended on the oxidation temperature.
The oxide layer had a single-layer structure at 1000 °C and a double-layer structure at 1300 °C.
With the increasing temperature, the degree of oxidation of metal elements was more complete and the oxide layer became thicker.

item.mechanism: Volume expansion during oxidation causes bulging and cracking in the oxide layer at lower temperatures (1000 °C), whereas volatilization of oxides at higher temperatures (1300 °C) balances volume changes.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating
item.supporting_observation: At 1000 °C, a gap and bulge appear between layers due to volume expansion; at 1300 °C, no gap exists because MoO3 volatilization reduces volume.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism relies on the specific volatility of MoO3, which is not mentioned for other alloy systems.
quotes: The swelling of the oxide layer may have been caused by volume expansion during oxidation.

The complete oxidation of the metal and silicon could cause a significant increase in the oxide layer volume, whereas the volatilization of some oxides (such as MoO 3 ) could cause the loss of the oxide layer and reduce the volume.
Consequently, the volume of the oxide layer was basically the same as that of the initial silicide layer.

item.mechanism: Silicon diffusion creates pores in the silicide layer as Si atoms leave the coating to enter the substrate.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating
item.supporting_observation: Many holes and cracks were found in the silicide layer, attributed to the diffusion of a large number of silicon atoms into the RHEA substrate.
item.scope_limits: The text does not specify if this pore formation occurs in the absence of oxidation or at different diffusion rates.
quotes: The pores formed in the silicide layer were resulted from the diffusion of a large number of silicon atoms into the RHEA substrate.
Many holes and cracks were found in the silicide layer.
The cracks were originated from the interface between the silicide and oxide layers and terminated at the interface between the silicide layer and REHA substrate.

item.mechanism: Cr and Fe elements diffuse into the substrate along with Si but at a much lower rate, leading to higher concentrations of Cr and Fe in the inner silicide layer.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating
item.supporting_observation: EDS analysis shows significantly higher Cr and Fe content in the inner low-silicon layer compared to the outer high-silicon layer.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is specific to the Si-20Cr-20Fe system; diffusion rates for other alloying elements are not discussed.
quotes: However, it should be noted that the contents of both Cr and Fe in the inner layer are much higher than those in the outer layer.
Some Cr and Fe elements spread to the RHEA substrate with the Si, but at a much lower diffusion rate than that of the Si element.
It is worth noting that the contents of Cr and Fe in the siliconized layer with a low content of silicon were significantly higher than those in the siliconized layer with a high content of silicon.

item.mechanism: The silicide coating effectively prevents oxidation of the underlying RHEA substrate by forming a protective oxide layer and maintaining structural integrity.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating
item.operating_conditions: High-temperature oxidation at 1000 °C and 1300 °C for 1 hour
item.supporting_observation: The uncoated side surfaces oxidized to form yellow oxide scales, while the coated surfaces maintained good integrity with a protective oxide layer.
item.scope_limits: The text states the coating prevents oxidation but does not quantify the protection efficiency or compare it to other coating types in this specific study.
quotes: The results show that the silicide coating could effectively prevent the oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA.
The uncoated side surfaces were oxidized to form a yellow oxide scale.
Both the oxidized silicide coatings maintained good integrity.

item.mechanism: The silicide layer maintains its double-layer structure (MSi2 outer, M5Si3 inner) during oxidation, even as it thickens and moves inward.
item.system: MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating
item.supporting_observation: XRD and EDS analysis confirm the L1 (M5Si3) and L2 (MSi2) layers persist after oxidation with similar compositions to the initial coating.
item.scope_limits: The text notes that Fe silicide was not detected, implying the mechanism might differ if Fe silicides were stable.
quotes: Compared with the initial silicified layer, its structure did not change significantly.
The double-layer structure of the siliconized layer oxidized at 1000 °C and 1300 °C was the same as the structure of the initial siliconized layer.
According to the analysis by EDS (see Table 2), L3 consisted of complex metal oxides and silicon dioxide.
